what: Documentation states what the code does, not what it might do
title: Rootopia
text: Descriptions, roxygen vignettes claims package must checkable source: describe capabilities planned, partial, read R/. feature incomplete, say plainly name . restate marketing lines (“track roots depth”). what: Spelling: en-US prose, but never rename code
title: Rootopia
text: DESCRIPTION declares Language: en-US, R CMD check ---cran spell-checks Title, Description every man/*.Rd . Write prose en-US: color, center, gray, behavior, neighbor, labeled, modeled, summarize, normalize, visualize, artifact, analyze (verb). Nouns spellings – analysis, analyses, characteristics – already correct; “fix” . applies prose . Never rewrite identifier match . spelling change safe comment, roxygen block, vignette, .Rd file message string. breaking change : argument name function another package, e.g. landscapemetrics::calculate_lsm(neighbourhood = 8); argument name, column name list element package returns, user code indexes ; literal must match something else, e.g. R color name col = "grey80", string compared match.arg(). exceptions live repo must stay spelled . bulk substitution, grep candidates check hit prose; hit sits inside call, string name, leave note .

title: Batch Processing with root_depth_metrics()
text: calc_root_order_metrics = TRUE builds segment graph skeleton image (via branch_order_map()) labels every root segment four order schemes — strahler_order order_from_tip per segment, root_max_order_from_tip order_from_base per continuous root. order_scheme picks one reported ; defaults "strahler_order", every distal unbranched root order 1 number rises two roots equal order meet. See Flatbed Scans vignette worked example underlying pipeline. adds two kinds columns: Per depth bin — branching order varies depth: scheme deprecated alias (branch_order, tip_order, root_order), column repeated name , code indexing either name finds . Per tube (repeated every row tube) — thickest order-1 path vs. higher-order branches, split order_metrics(..., groups = "thickest"): Slow. builds one segment graph per image, considerably expensive metric groups. Disable (default) quick exploratory runs enable need architectural detail.
code: result <- root_depth_metrics(   path_seg                = "scans/segmented/2022_02/",   path_skl                = "scans/skeleton/2022_02/",   session                 = "2022_02",   calc_root_order_metrics = TRUE ) library(ggplot2)  ggplot(result, aes(x = depth, y = lateral_root_fraction, color = Tube)) +   geom_line() +   geom_point() +   coord_flip() +   scale_x_reverse() +   theme_minimal() +   labs(     title = "Lateral Root Fraction by Depth",     x     = "Soil Depth (cm)",     y     = "Fraction of ordered skeleton pixels outside the main-root class"   )

code: order_res <- branch_order_map(   skel  = skl,    # skeleton from step 2   mask  = seg,    # filled root mask, same grid — used for diameters   order = "order_from_base",   unit  = "cm",   dpi   = 150 )  # One row per order class: total length, mean diameter, tips, branch points order_res$summary  # Rasterised branch-order classes, aligned to the skeleton zoom_plot(order_res$class_map, main = "Branch order") main_vs_lateral <- order_metrics(order_res, groups = "thickest") print(main_vs_lateral)  # Fraction of total root length in higher-order branches (order >= 2) lateral_length_fraction <- main_vs_lateral$length_fraction[main_vs_lateral$group == "rest"] # Per-order-class table (same as order_res$summary), with a running total of # length across the orders in `cumulative_length` order_metrics(order_res)  # Order 1 (thickest central path) vs. everything else order_metrics(order_res, groups = list(main = 1))  # Two named sets; any remaining order still shows up as `rest` order_metrics(order_res, groups = list(main = 1, fine = 2:3)) order_res2 <- branch_order_map(   skel          = skl,   mask          = seg,   order         = "order_from_base",   unit          = "cm",   dpi           = 300,   overlay_png   = "branch_order_overlay.png" )  # Zoom into a 200x200 px window at 3x magnification plot_order_window(   order_res2$edges, skl,   r_range = c(100, 300), c_range = c(100, 300),   scale = 3, file = "branch_order_window.png" )

code: z  <- seq(0, 60, by = 5)                    # 13 intervals, 5 cm each  # A surface-weighted reference, with no mass below 25 cm. Keeping the support # in the upper half of the grid matters: a profile shifted past the bottom of # the grid loses the mass that falls off, and renormalizing what is left # changes its shape, so it is no longer the same profile moved down. p0 <- exp(-abs(z - 10) / 7) p0[z > 25] <- 0 reference <- p0 / sum(p0)  # Move the whole profile down by k intervals. shift_by <- function(p, k) c(rep(0, k), head(p, length(p) - k))  shifted10 <- shift_by(reference, 2)         # 2 intervals = 10 cm shifted35 <- shift_by(reference, 7)         # 7 intervals = 35 cm even      <- rep(1 / length(z), length(z))  # equal root in every interval  # A two-layer profile: a surface mode and a second one at 45 cm. The weight on # the deep mode is solved so this profile has exactly the reference's mean # rooting depth -- same center of mass, different shape. shallow <- exp(-z / 5);           shallow[z > 15] <- 0 deep    <- exp(-abs(z - 45) / 7); deep[z < 30]    <- 0 shallow <- shallow / sum(shallow) deep    <- deep / sum(deep)  mean_depth <- function(p) sum(z * p) w <- (mean_depth(reference) - mean_depth(shallow)) /      (mean_depth(deep)      - mean_depth(shallow)) bimodal <- (1 - w) * shallow + w * deep  # The package function, with the depth of each bin as `index` and no tail # weighting, so every centimeter of depth counts the same. The result is in the # units of `index`, which is centimeters here. emd_cm <- function(a, b)   compare_depth_distribution(a, b, metric = "wasserstein", index = z,                              tail_weight = FALSE)  compare_panel <- function(b, label_b, title) {   Fa <- cumsum(reference)   Fb <- cumsum(b)   plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = rev(range(z)),        xlab = "cumulative share", ylab = "depth (cm)", main = title)   graphics::polygon(c(Fa, rev(Fb)), c(z, rev(z)), col = "grey88",                     border = NA)   graphics::lines(Fa, z, col = "steelblue4", lwd = 2)   graphics::lines(Fb, z, col = "coral3",     lwd = 2)   graphics::legend("bottomright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, cex = 0.8,                    col = c("steelblue4", "coral3"),                    legend = c("reference", label_b))   graphics::mtext(sprintf("%.1f cm to move", emd_cm(reference, b)),                   side = 3, line = -1.3, cex = 0.75) }  op <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1)) compare_panel(shifted10, "10 cm deeper",      "same shape, 10 cm down") compare_panel(shifted35, "35 cm deeper",      "same shape, 35 cm down") compare_panel(even, "equal at all depths",    "spread evenly") compare_panel(bimodal, "bimodal",            "same mean depth, other shape") graphics::par(op) c(reference = mean_depth(reference), bimodal = mean_depth(bimodal)) #> reference   bimodal  #>  10.68323  10.68323 emd_cm(reference, bimodal) #> [1] 9.669479

code: data(flatbed_scan_example)  seg_fb <- load_flexible_image(flatbed_scan_example, output_format = "spatrast",                               scale = "binary", select_layer = 2)  # The top edge of the scan carries an artifact rather than root. Anything # non-root that touches the mask can join otherwise separate roots into one # component and move the base each path is measured from, so it goes before # anything is traced. e <- terra::ext(seg_fb) seg_fb <- terra::crop(seg_fb, terra::ext(e[1], e[2], e[3],                                         e[4] - 0.05 * (e[4] - e[3])))  fb_clean <- clean_image(seg_fb,                         fill_holes_upto   = 50,                         drop_objects_upto = 50,                         protect_border    = FALSE)  fb_skl <- skeletonize_image(fb_clean, verbose = FALSE)  # The order map is built on the unpruned skeleton. Pruning removes short # terminal branches, and which end of the order scale that affects depends on # the scheme: under order_from_base, used below, terminal segments carry the # highest numbers, so pruning first flattens the top of the classification. # `prune_skeleton()` is still the right call before counting tips, and # `prune_terminal_segments()` prunes inside the graph if you want both. fb_skl_pruned <- prune_skeleton(fb_skl, mask = fb_clean, min_length = 50,                                 iter = 1)  # The segment graph over a whole tray is the slowest step in this article. order_res <- branch_order_map(   skel  = fb_skl,   mask  = fb_clean,          # the mask is what supplies diameters   order = "order_from_base",   unit  = "cm",   dpi   = 1200 ) #> Cropped to 1900x1964 (offset 0,36) #> Distance transform... #> Tracing + contracting junctions... #>   111 segment(s) #>   spliced pass-through nodes: 111 -> 111 segment(s) #>   resolved crossings: 111 -> 111 segment(s) #> Tip order... #> Done in 0.40s. 111 segments, max order 8, total length 7857.9 px  # One window for every figure in this part, so the panels can be compared. fb_frac <- 0.25 fb_ctr  <- c(0.7, 0.625)  zoom_plot(seg_fb,   main = "Segmented, as it comes", frac = fb_frac,           center = fb_ctr, overview = FALSE) zoom_plot(fb_clean, main = "Cleaned", frac = fb_frac, center = fb_ctr) zoom_plot(fb_skl_pruned, main = "Skeleton (spurs pruned)", frac = fb_frac,           center = fb_ctr) # render_order_overlay() writes the figure with grDevices::png(), which can # emit a palette image; terra then reads it as a single band of palette # indices rather than three color bands. png::readPNG() expands the palette, # so build the raster from that array and zoom_plot() it like any other image. as_rgb_rast <- function(file) {   a <- png::readPNG(file)                        # values in 0-1   if (length(dim(a)) == 2L) a <- array(a, c(dim(a), 3L))   r <- terra::rast(a[, , 1:3, drop = FALSE] * 255)   terra::RGB(r) <- 1:3   r }  ord_png <- tempfile(fileext = ".png") render_order_overlay(attr(order_res$edges, "segments"),                      order_res$edges$order_from_base,                      attr(order_res$edges, "dims"), ord_png,                      mask = fb_clean, value_label = "order from base")  # overview = FALSE: the whole tray at page width shows nothing, so only the # magnified window is drawn. zoom_plot(as_rgb_rast(ord_png), frac = fb_frac, center = fb_ctr,           maxcell = Inf, overview = FALSE, main = "Order from base") win_png <- tempfile(fileext = ".png") plot_order_window(order_res$edges, fb_skl,                   r_range = c(600, 1000), c_range = c(900, 1300),                   scale = 2, file = win_png,                   order_col = "order_from_base")  if (requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE)) {   op <- graphics::par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))   plot(grDevices::as.raster(png::readPNG(win_png)))   graphics::par(op) } order_res$summary #>   order n_segments n_tips n_branch_points total_length cumulative_length #> 1     1         26      6              22   5.16391097          5.163911 #> 2     2         38     25              13   3.30586934          8.469780 #> 3     3         27     15              14   4.75573400         13.225514 #> 4     4         14     12               2   0.71618856         13.941703 #> 5     5          4      2               2   1.91089531         15.852598 #> 6     6          2      2               0   0.04935045         15.901949 #>   cumulative_fraction mean_segment_length branching_frequency mean_diameter #> 1           0.3247345          0.19861196            4.260337    0.06893584 #> 2           0.5326253          0.08699656            3.932400    0.04545475 #> 3           0.8316914          0.17613830            2.943815    0.06355430 #> 4           0.8767292          0.05115633            2.792561    0.04367593 #> 5           0.9968966          0.47772383            1.046630    0.04563837 #> 6           1.0000000          0.02467522            0.000000    0.03223201 #>   median_diameter #> 1      0.06845654 #> 2      0.04095795 #> 3      0.04190786 #> 4      0.03722479 #> 5      0.03825043 #> 6      0.03160465  # The thickest order class against everything else, picked by diameter rather # than by order number, so the same call means the same thing across a dataset. order_metrics(order_res, groups = "thickest") #>      group    orders n_segments n_tips n_branch_points total_length #> 1 thickest         1         26      6              22     5.163911 #> 2     rest 2,3,4,5,6         85     56              31    10.738038 #>   length_fraction mean_segment_length branching_frequency mean_diameter #> 1       0.3247345           0.1986120            4.260337    0.06893584 #> 2       0.6752655           0.1263299            2.886933    0.05332406 #>   median_diameter #> 1      0.06845654 #> 2      0.03993719 diam_fb   <- root_diameter(fb_clean, skeleton_img = fb_skl_pruned,                            unit = "cm", dpi = 1200, select_layer = NULL) diam_vals <- diam_fb$diameters      # the per-skeleton-pixel values  cat(sprintf("diameter mean %.4f cm | sd %.4f | max %.4f cm\n",             mean(diam_vals), stats::sd(diam_vals), max(diam_vals))) #> diameter mean 0.0618 cm | sd 0.0164 | max 0.1108 cm  ggplot(data.frame(diameter = diam_vals), aes(x = diameter)) +   geom_histogram(bins = 24, fill = "steelblue4", color = "white") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(x = "Diameter (cm)", y = "Count",        title = "Root diameter distribution")

code: net <- network_metrics(order_res$edges, topology = "projected_tree") net$traits #> $n_nodes #> [1] 115 #>  #> $n_edges #> [1] 111 #>  #> $n_components #> [1] 4 #>  #> $n_tips #> [1] 62 #>  #> $n_branch_points #> [1] 53 #>  #> $tip_ratio #> [1] 0.5391304 #>  #> $beta #> [1] 0.9652174 #>  #> $total_length #> [1] 15.90195 #>  #> $mean_edge_length #> [1] 0.1432608 net$qc #> $cyclomatic #> [1] 0 #>  #> $alpha_meshedness #> [1] 0 #>  #> $gamma #> [1] 0.3274336 #>  #> $n_self_loops #> [1] 0 #>  #> $n_duplicate_edges #> [1] 0 #>  #> $is_forest #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $artefact_cycles #> [1] 0 #>  #> $artefact_rate #> [1] 0 net$note #> [1] "loops in a projected tree are crossings the segmentation did not separate; artefact_rate divides that count by network length, in whatever unit the edge table carries, so images can be compared" et <- root_transport(order_res$edges) head(et[, c("length", "path_length", "path_resistance",             "downstream_tips", "downstream_length")], 4) #>       length path_length path_resistance downstream_tips downstream_length #> 1 0.04264472    2.221137         6827712               1        0.04264472 #> 2 0.04009685    2.218590         6929970               1        0.04009685 #> 3 0.18486079    2.178493         6337904               2        0.26760236 #> 4 0.04135668    2.034989         6777683               1        0.04135668 png_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")  # max_side caps the longest side of the written PNG, and anything below the # scan's own width throws pixels away: thin roots drop out rather than getting # thicker. Keep it at the full width and zoom afterwards instead. # A handful of thin distal segments carry resistance far above the rest, and a # ramp stretched to that maximum leaves every other segment in nearly the same # color. Capping the value at the 97th percentile spends the ramp on the range # the roots actually occupy; the capped segments sit at the top color. The # alternative is to paint log10(path_resistance) and label the bar as a log # scale, which keeps the extremes distinguishable but makes the bar harder to # read as a physical quantity. cap <- stats::quantile(et$path_resistance, 0.97, na.rm = TRUE)  render_order_overlay(attr(et, "segments"),                      pmin(et$path_resistance, cap),                      attr(et, "dims"), png_file,                      mask = fb_clean, max_side = 2000,                      value_label = "path resistance (capped at p97)")  zoom_plot(as_rgb_rast(png_file), frac = fb_frac, center = fb_ctr,           maxcell = Inf, overview = FALSE, main = "Path resistance") op     <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1)) pt_bg  <- grDevices::rgb(0.21, 0.35, 0.47, 0.45) pt_cex <- 0.4 + 2.4 * et$mean_diameter / max(et$mean_diameter, na.rm = TRUE)  plot(et$path_length, et$path_resistance,      pch = 21, bg = pt_bg, col = "steelblue4", cex = pt_cex,      xlab = "path length from the base (cm)",      ylab = "path resistance (relative)",      main = "linear resistance axis")  plot(et$path_length, et$path_resistance, log = "y",      pch = 21, bg = pt_bg, col = "steelblue4", cex = pt_cex,      xlab = "path length from the base (cm)",      ylab = "path resistance (relative, log)",      main = "log resistance axis") graphics::par(op)

title: Rotation Bias and Rhythmicity Analysis with Rootopia
text: vignette demonstrates detect correct rotational bias minirhizotron setups using Rootopia package. minirhizotron studies, scanner tube inserted angle soil can rotate slightly sessions. CI-600 similar scanners cover full 360° arc, sequential images tube may perfectly overlap. Left uncorrected, rotation introduces systematic spatial bias — roots near scan edges observed sessions others. Rootopia addresses four functions: estimate_rotation_center() — locates rotational zero point tape coverage single image estimate_rotation_shift() — quantifies pixel offset two sessions using image correlation rotation_censor() — crops images shared, overlap region slice_rotation() — splits tube surface slices along rotation axis (circumference), root traits can summarized separately slice last point matters beyond rotation correction : tube circumference split slices, rhythmicity() / fit_sine_curve() family — normally introduced time-series data — can applied sequence per-slice root traits test whether roots distributed evenly around tube circumference, whether systematic top-/ side--side pattern (e.g. roots underside tube). spatial, temporal, application functions — see Circumferential zoning rhythmicity section .

text: rotation_censor() crops image rows present every session retained. eliminates non-overlapping margins makes root counts directly comparable across sessions. Two modes available: fixed_rotation = FALSE — cuts proportionally based measured offset; output width varies fixed_rotation = TRUE — centers crop specified row forces fixed output width; recommended comparing multiple sessions  Note tube geometry. inner outer tube diameters differ, observed root length slightly underestimates true root length soil. resize coefficient may applied separately; rotation_censor() handle correction.

text: rgb_Oulanka2023_Session03_T067 real RGB tube scan. cut overlapping pieces, save little “tube” folder, let stitch_root_scans() reassemble — exactly path scans take.  band searched twice overlap, report’s overlap column still comes back ov: search area upper bound overlap, overlap . two panels indistinguishable. (chunk needs suggested png package write demo files.)
code: data("rgb_Oulanka2023_Session03_T067")  # load to an (H, W, C) array; downsampled here only to keep the vignette light img <- load_flexible_image(rgb_Oulanka2023_Session03_T067,                            output_format = "array", normalize = FALSE) #> Warning: `normalize`, `binarize`, and `denormalize` are deprecated; use `scale` #> ("to_01", "to_255", "binary", "none") instead. img <- img[seq(1, nrow(img), 3), seq(1, ncol(img), 3), , drop = FALSE] dim(img)                                   # rows (rotation) x cols (length) x RGB #> [1]  387 1633    3 W       <- ncol(img) piece_w <- W %/% 3L                        # each piece ~1/3 of the length ov      <- piece_w %/% 4L                  # overlap = 25% of a piece step    <- piece_w - ov starts  <- (0:((W - piece_w) %/% step)) * step pieces  <- lapply(starts, function(s) img[, (s + 1):(s + piece_w), , drop = FALSE]) length(pieces)                             # number of overlapping frames #> [1] 3 # save the pieces as one tube ("T067") in a temp folder, as if freshly scanned d  <- file.path(tempdir(), "stitch_demo") dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE) sc <- if (max(img, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) 255 else 1 for (i in seq_along(pieces)) {   png::writePNG(pmin(pmax(pieces[[i]] / sc, 0), 1),                 file.path(d, sprintf("Oulanka_T067_%02d.png", i))) } list.files(d) #> [1] "Oulanka_T067_01.png" "Oulanka_T067_02.png" "Oulanka_T067_03.png" res <- stitch_root_scans(d, pattern = ".png", edge_width = 2L * ov,                          vertical_region = nrow(img), vertical_offset = 0,                          report = TRUE, verbose = FALSE) mosaic <- res$mosaics[["T067"]] dim(mosaic)            # reconstructed length #> [1]  387 1360    3 res$report             # per-join dx, dy, peak (confidence), overlap #>   tube step  dx dy        peak overlap #> 1 T067    1 136  0 0.001681298     136 #> 2 T067    2 136  0 0.001614661     136 norm01 <- function(a) a / max(a, na.rm = TRUE)         # display only span   <- ncol(mosaic)  op <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(0, 0, 1.4, 0)) plot(grDevices::as.raster(norm01(img[, seq_len(span), , drop = FALSE]))) graphics::title("original scan (cropped to the stitched span)") plot(grDevices::as.raster(norm01(mosaic))) graphics::title("re-stitched by stitch_root_scans()") graphics::par(op)

Raise vertical_offset skip header, label, tape strip top. direction — "horizontal" (default, frames side--side) "vertical" (frames stacked top--bottom, e.g. strips acquired tube). method — "phase" (FFT phase correlation) method implemented. title: Stitching Scan Sequences into Mosaics with Rootopia
text: Grouping — group_regex. regular expression pulls tube id path; files sharing id form one sequence. default "T0\\d{2}" (\\ R string-escaping regex T0\d{2}) matches T0 plus two digits, e.g. T067. Adapt names, use NULL put every file single mosaic: Selecting — select vs tubes. select indexes sorted file list grouping; tubes selects whole tubes index, name, interactively. tubes = "ask" prints available tubes indices; pass index range, error names many called. Normally want tubes; select raw file ranges. Ordering — order_by / decreasing. Frames within tube stitched order, decides sequence. default key file name, sorts lexicographically — unpadded numbers come wrong (_10 _2). order_by takes regular expression sorts match instead; match parses number sorts numerically. decreasing = TRUE reverses , frames numbered far end tube back: file pattern match stops run rather placed arbitrarily, since frame wrong part sequence exactly failure argument exists prevent. (Equivalently, zero-pad frame numbers — _02, _10 — default name sort already correct.) Output names — out_prefix / out_format. out_dir set, mosaic written <out_dir>/<out_prefix><tube>.<ext>. out_prefix tags session/site separate runs don’t collide; out_format picks "png" (default) "tiff":
code: group_regex = "T\\d+"          # T1, T67, T123 group_regex = "tube[-_]?\\d+"  # tube12 / tube_12 / tube-12 group_regex = NULL             # no grouping -> one mosaic stitch_root_scans("scans", pattern = ".tiff", select = 1:36)              # first 36 files stitch_root_scans("scans", pattern = ".tiff", tubes  = 1:36)              # first 36 tubes stitch_root_scans("scans", pattern = ".tiff", tubes  = c("T037", "T040")) # named tubes stitch_root_scans("scans", pattern = ".tiff", tubes  = "ask")             # interactive # order by the number just before the extension, e.g. ..._02.tiff, ..._10.tiff stitch_root_scans("scans", pattern = ".tiff", order_by = "\\d+(?=\\.)") stitch_root_scans("scans", pattern = ".tiff", order_by = "\\d+(?=\\.)", decreasing = TRUE) stitch_root_scans("scans/Oulanka2020_November", pattern = ".tiff",                   out_dir = "mosaics", out_prefix = "Oulanka2020_Session03_",                   out_format = "tiff") # -> mosaics/Oulanka2020_Session03_T067.tif, ...T068.tif, ...

Every terminal segment order 1; peeling terminals away round round, segment's order 1 + max(child orders). rises toward interior, distal end even thick root 1. count runs tips inward (centripetal), direction root ecology's morphometric classification uses, strict Strahler ordering: increments every junction, axis carrying ten single laterals reaches 11. strahler_order (per segment) peeling strict rule: segment's order rises two children share highest order, otherwise inherits order unchanged. lone thin lateral joining thick axis leaves axis . root_max_order_from_tip (per root) count . Segments grouped continuous roots (continuation rule ) every segment root takes largest order_from_tip found along – , since column never falls move basally, value root's basal end. thick main axis therefore keeps high value tip instead dropping 1. Sensitive deep deepest subtree runs. order_from_base (per root) Generation counting, direction developmental classification uses. thickest root (length-weighted mean diameter) connected component order 1; counting branching hops outward, laterals 2, 3, . Independent subtree depth, one heavily branched root inflate rest. Order 1 chosen thickness, knowing root grew first. tip_order, root_order branch_order deprecated aliases order_from_tip, root_max_order_from_tip order_from_base. $edges carries copies columns, order, order_col value accept . text: Performs three sequential cleaning operations binary segmented image: Hole filling – fills black regions enclosed white (segmentation gaps inside roots). Small holes inside root inflate local distance values force medial axis bifurcate around hole, producing spurious branching points.  Isolated artifact pixels produce phantom skeleton segments.  Cleaning first yields much cleaner skeleton.

Superseded geometry, kept existing code runs unchanged: TRUE means geometry = "tube", FALSE means geometry = "window". Ignored geometry given. tube_thicc Numeric; diameter minirhizotron tube cm. Used geometry = "tube" tilt Numeric. Superseded angle_from_vertical, states convention name. Degrees horizontal, opposite reference, tilt = t angle_from_vertical = 90 - t. Given , conversion applied warning says . 45 angle either way dpi Numeric; image resolution dots per inch start_soil Numeric; soil surface boundary cm (0 = surface) center_offset Numeric [0, 1]; top tube – shallowest line curvature wave – sits across image height, fraction one full tube circumference. 0 puts first row, 0.5 halfway , 1 last row. 0 1 point tube, image seam. Used geometry = "tube" geometry Character; shape imaged. One "tube" (default), "window" "flat" – see Geometries. angle_from_vertical Numeric; insertion angle degrees measured vertical, [0, 90]. 0 upright tube 90 horizontal one, number far tube leans – convention field notes usually record ("installed 45 degrees"). Used geometry = "tube" "window". angle splits tube's depth two axes, two terms complements. depth gained along tube's length scales cos(angle_from_vertical): upright tube gains full centimeter depth per centimeter tube, horizontal one gains none. depth spread around circumference scales sin(angle_from_vertical): upright tube's cross-section horizontal, whole circumference sits one depth, horizontal tube's upper side full diameter lower side.

Freeman methods treat skeleton discrete chain-code path: freeman_basic: L = sqrt(2) * Nd + freeman_corrected: L = 0.948 * (sqrt(2) * Nd + ) Kimura methods treat skeleton discretized representation underlying continuous curve reduce orientation bias: kimura1: L = sqrt(Nd^2 + (Nd + )^2) kimura2 (default): L = sqrt(Nd^2 + (Nd + /2)^2) + /2 Kimura2 estimator generally preferred due improved stability across object orientations curvature distributions.

title: Stitch two scans into one mosaic with linear feather blending — stitch_image_pair
text: img1, img2 Image inputs (file path, SpatRaster, Raster*, cimg, magick-image, matrix, array). See load_flexible_image supported formats. method Alignment method. Currently "phase" (FFT phase correlation) supported. "feature" (SIFT/ORB keypoint matching Python original) requires OpenCV CRAN-compatible R backend; raises informative error. edge_width Width pixels band searched overlap, overlap . Clamped narrower frame. least wide true overlap, overlap wider band falls outside part frames compared reported smaller one. Beyond upper bound: band many times overlap still locates , cost larger transform. overlap unknown, set largest overlap frames plausibly . vertical_region Height pixels vertical band used alignment. vertical_offset Starting row (top) vertical band. direction "horizontal" (default, frames side side) "vertical" (frames stacked top bottom, e.g. minirhizotron strips acquired tube). Vertical transposes inputs, runs horizontal core, transposes result back. preprocess Preprocessing applied edge bands correlation: one "none" (default), "center" (subtract mean), "norm" (divide SD), "center_norm", "hann" (demean + Hann window), "grad" (gradient magnitude) "grad_norm". "hann", "grad" "center" help scans uneven lighting sparse texture; "norm" alone barely changes phase correlation (already scale-invariant). well-textured scans "none" usually fine. blend overlap band combined: "linear" (default, alpha ramp 1 -> 0, good color scans), "overlay" (img2 hides img1), "overlay_first" (img1 hides img2), "max" (lighten / union - recommended segmented/binary masks, averaging make fractional values ghost thin roots) "min" (darken). blend_width Optional width (px) linear ramp, centered overlap (hard img1 left, hard img2 right); NULL (default) ramps across whole overlap. smaller value reduces root ghosting color scans. Ignored unless blend = "linear". min_overlap, max_overlap Bounds pixels overlap look . peak read columns correlation surface correspond overlap min_overlap max_overlap pixels, overlap outside bracket never returned. defaults 0 Inf leave ends open search whole band. max_overlap clamped band width, since band express wider overlap; min_overlap wider band, max_overlap one pixel, error rather silently empty search.
